2. Typed Workflow Lisp provenance (item 8), TDD. Add an optional frontend_kind parameter to elaborate_surface_workflow and pass it into WorkflowProvenance. In the lowering path, pass frontend_kind="workflow_lisp" where the surface is elaborated just before build_loaded_workflow_bundle, so every lowered or validated bundle from compile_stage3_entrypoint, including imported Workflow Lisp bundles, carries it. Do not touch classic-YAML bundles that come in through imported_workflow_bundles; they must stay linked as the same object. In build_frontend_bundle, replace(...) must keep selected_bundle.provenance.frontend_kind instead of overwriting it. Then change CallExecutor._is_workflow_lisp_target to return provenance.frontend_kind == "workflow_lisp" and delete the .orc suffix check. Tests: lowered entry, imported .orc and pass-through YAML provenance (the YAML bundle is the same object); a .orc-named YAML bundle is not Workflow Lisp. Files: orchestrator/workflow/elaboration.py, orchestrator/workflow_lisp/lowering/core.py, orchestrator/workflow_lisp/build.py, orchestrator/workflow/calls.py, tests/test_workflow_lisp_build_artifacts.py, tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py.

3. Classic-YAML duplicate import alias detection (item 5), TDD. New module orchestrator/workflow/yaml_import_aliases.py (about 100 lines). It runs yaml.compose(text, Loader=PreservingLoader) and walks the top-level MappingNode. It collects every `imports` key node, both direct keys and keys from top-level `<<` merge sources, and every alias key inside each imports mapping, expanding `<<` merges there too. It reports `imports.<alias>: duplicate import alias` once per repeated alias with each occurrence as `line L, column C` (start_mark + 1). It reports `imports: duplicate top-level mapping` once, with each imports key position, only when the sections are repeated and every alias is distinct. In WorkflowLoader._load_workflow, read the file text once, run the check before yaml.load, and on errors call _add_error and return {} so build_loaded_workflow_bundle is never reached. load_bundle then raises WorkflowValidationError. Tests (new tests/test_loader_import_aliases.py, through WorkflowLoader.load with build_loaded_workflow_bundle patched to fail if called): duplicate keys, a merge inside imports, repeated sections with a shared alias, repeated sections with distinct aliases, top-level merge sources, and a single merged section that still loads. Files: orchestrator/workflow/yaml_import_aliases.py, orchestrator/loader.py, tests/test_loader_import_aliases.py.

4. Projection support data. Add an import_alias field to CallBoundaryProjection, keyword-constructible and defaulting to None so existing constructors still work. In lowering.py register_call_boundary, populate it from the call step's authored `call` alias. The auditor needs the declared exhaustion range and must not re-read the workflow. 5. Loop bookkeeping validation (item 3). New module orchestrator/workflow/resume_loop_progress.py (under 500 lines). It defines ResumeProjectionValidationError(ValueError) with .reason and .message, where str() is the message, and state_projection.py re-exports it. It also defines pure validators: validate_for_each_progress(name, progress) (unique non-bool non-negative indices within items; current_index in range and not already completed) and validate_repeat_until_progress(name, progress, max_iterations, loop_step_row). The repeat_until validator admits exactly the four forms: active; terminal condition success; successful exhaustion with exhausted:true and a completed loop step; failed exhaustion with exhausted absent or false and a failed loop step whose error.type is repeat_until_iterations_exhausted. Every message is the exact literal listed under enumerate_resume_slots. Each validator returns the iteration indices whose loop-local candidates exist. Tests: a table-driven test per message, plus one per admitted form, in tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py through enumerate_resume_slots (step 6). Files: orchestrator/workflow/resume_loop_progress.py, orchestrator/workflow/state_projection.py, tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py.

6. Slot index and resolvers on WorkflowStateProjection. To keep state_projection.py under 500 lines, put the frozen dataclasses (ResumeProjectionSlot with node_id, step_id, presentation_key, region, iteration_index; ResumeProjectionSlotIndex; ResumeIdentityResolution; ResumeCallBoundaryResolution) and the enumeration logic in a new module, orchestrator/workflow/resume_slots.py, with thin methods on WorkflowStateProjection. enumerate_resume_slots(state): build candidates for top-level and finalization entries from the projection tables, then loop-local and loop-contained call candidates only for iterations admitted by the step 5 validators, using projection.step_key, runtime_step_id and CallBoundaryProjection.runtime_step_id(i) (no id string parsing). Build call_boundaries_by_step_id. Collect unclaimed_explicit_rows as (row name, snapshotted step_id) pairs for steps.* rows with an explicit step_id that no candidate's presentation key claims; this must tolerate unhashable ids. The method never mutates or backfills state. resolve_resume_step_id(slot_index, step_id, presentation_key=None): unhashable or malformed id gives count 0; with presentation_key it reports exact_identity_candidate_count. resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, call_step_id) takes positional arguments. Tests: valid, stale, loop-local, finalization, loop-contained call and unhashable ids, plus a no-mutation assertion (deepcopy equality). Files: orchestrator/workflow/resume_slots.py, orchestrator/workflow/state_projection.py, tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py.

7. Retry lineage (item 4). New module orchestrator/workflow/resume_retry_lineage.py with RetryFrameMember (frame_id, ordinal), CompletedFrameMember (frame_id), CallFrameRetryLineage (base_frame_id, completed_members, failed_predecessors in ordinal order, running_member), CallFrameRetryLineageError(ValueError) with .reason, index_retry_lineage(boundary_step_id, frame_items, *, frontend_kind) and next_unused_retry_frame_id(lineage). Parse `::retry::<n>` with an exact suffix rule: a positive decimal ordinal; a malformed or nested marker raises unsupported_shape. Map other failures as follows: mixed bases, several running members, a duplicate ordinal, or several non-completed frames on a non-Workflow-Lisp boundary raise ambiguous_resumable_call_frame; a missing ordinal or unknown status raises unsupported_shape; a call_step_id that is not the boundary raises missing_call_boundary; differing aliases raise persisted_import_alias_mismatch. The next retry id is the lowest unused positive ordinal over all members, completed ones included. Re-export everything from resume_projection_integrity (step 8). Tests (new tests/test_resume_retry_lineage.py): each reason, ordinal ordering, idempotent allocation, a completed frame filling a gap, and the non-Workflow-Lisp single running member. Files: orchestrator/workflow/resume_retry_lineage.py, tests/test_resume_retry_lineage.py.

8. Auditor module (items 1, 2, 7). New module orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py (under 500 lines; it imports nothing that loads files, checksums or migration evidence). It contains: ResumeScopePath (frozen; root(), child(), projection_scope, as_context(); a list input is snapshotted to a tuple in __post_init__); ResumeProjectionIntegrityError(ValueError) with .error; a single _diagnostic(reason, scope_path, bundle, state, field, offending_value, candidate_count, call_boundary_step_id) builder that emits all eight context keys and nulls container values; and audit_scope(bundle, state, scope_path). audit_scope checks, in order: steps/call_frames/frame shapes; enumerate_resume_slots, with ResumeProjectionValidationError mapped to unsupported_shape or invalid_loop_progress; each present steps.<name>.step_id (unknown, presentation mismatch, unclaimed; an absent id stays compatible and nothing is backfilled); current_step.step_id (missing_required_identity, out_of_scope, presentation mismatch); then for each call frame: call_step_id via a single resolve_call_boundary per caller identity (missing or out-of-scope, missing_call_boundary, ambiguous_call_boundary), import_alias against boundary.import_alias, the boundary alias present in the bundle imports (missing_imported_bundle), and index_retry_lineage per boundary using the imported bundle's frontend_kind. audit_scope does not recurse into child state; reached calls do that (step 10). Re-export the step 7 lineage API. 10. Reached-call integration (items 1 and 4). Add `from .resume_projection_integrity import audit_scope` at module level in calls.py (tests substitute this name), keeping the new logic in a helper module orchestrator/workflow/call_resume_audit.py so calls.py does not grow much past its current 982 lines. In execute_call, during resume: first, before lineage grouping, reject a completed frame whose id equals the frame the call would occupy, using resume_state_invalid_result with detail completed_call_frame_id_collision and exactly the specified context. Replace the first-non-completed frame_id_with_overrides scan and _retry_frame_id/_retry_family_base with resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, call_step_id) against the parent projection: exactly one boundary is required, and its import_alias selects the callee bundle while the persisted alias is only checked. Then call index_retry_lineage over the frames for that boundary. Keep the ordinary visit/start publication, authored/managed input, write-root, checksum and resume-bound-input validation in their current order. Carry the scope path on the executor/state manager (frame_id chain) for nested recursion. Return a projection failure as the failed call-step result carrying the exact diagnostic. In executor.py's finalization path and _execute_epilogue, never replace or clear a projection run error (_finalization_failure_error and the completed-path state.pop('error') must not touch it); if the projection error arises only in finalization it becomes the run error. Tests (tests/test_resume_command.py direct-executor section and tests/test_structured_control_flow.py): checksum envelope for each reason with a three-field diff; second-audit failure with open session metadata kept; success/failure/always routes, on_error=continue and loop continuation all stop; finalization failure supplemental; projection error inside finalization only; and an ordering test substituting executor.audit_scope to assert it runs before the prologue. findings: Must fix — Steps 10–11 contradict the required three-field integrity-failure envelope. Reaching CallExecutor.execute_call already follows _increment_step_visit, which persists step_visits (executor.py:2966,3554); the plan then persists a failed call-step result and may update finalization before promoting its error. A stale callee-local identity therefore changes more than root status, error, and updated_at. Audit reached child frames before parent visit/start/result publication, or define and implement an atomic rollback that restores the complete pre-resume state on integrity failure.

Must fix — The proposed retry index groups every frame with the same call_step_id and rejects mixed bases (steps 7–8, 10). A valid call reached twice through goto has frame IDs such as root.call::visit::1 and root.call::visit::2, both retained in call_frames; auditing the second visit would label the different visit bases ambiguous. Select the active visit family using the current call's visit identity while independently validating older families.

Must fix — The exact ::retry::<n> suffix parser in step 7 does not account for nested frame IDs. frame_id_with_overrides prefixes a nested call with its parent frame ID (calls.py:157–178); if the parent is root.call::visit::1::retry::1, a child ID contains ::retry::1 before its own local suffix. The proposed malformed/nested-marker rule rejects an ordinary nested call during a Workflow Lisp retry. Parse retry ordinals relative to the local frame segment or carry typed ancestry separately.

Must fix — StateManager.load deserializes before either planned audit, and RunState.from_dict requires workflow_file/workflow_checksum and unpacks each for_each value with ** (state.py:153–188,315–332). Missing checksum/path cannot reach the four reasoned checksum envelope in step 11, and a malformed for_each container raises KeyError/TypeError/AttributeError before audit_scope can return resume_projection_integrity_error. Add a raw-state or tolerant decode boundary that lets the guard classify these shapes before normal RunState construction.

Must fix — The second root audit can fail after the CLI has persisted observability overrides and opened an executor session (resume.py:389–590; plan step 12). Its finally block closes the session with _write_state, which changes runtime_observability and serializes RunState.to_dict, dropping unknown root keys. Thus the planned race test cannot also satisfy the stated three-field-only envelope or unknown-field preservation. Keep the second guard ahead of these writes, or make the mutation contract explicitly different and test it.

Must fix — Step 10 sends a completed-frame ID collision through resume_state_invalid_result, whose error type is call_resume_state_invalid (calls.py:560–575). This is a persisted call-frame identity failure, yet it bypasses the required single resume_projection_integrity_error and can follow ordinary call failure routing. Emit the same integrity diagnostic and make it sticky at the root.

Must fix — The auditor in step 8 checks frame call_step_id and import_alias but omits the persisted frame['call_frame_id'] and frame['call_step_name']; _CallFrameStateManager._snapshot writes both (call_frame_state.py:148–158). A frame keyed by a valid ID can carry a different embedded call_frame_id and pass the proposed checks, leaving one persisted identity unaudited. Check embedded IDs/names against the key and resolved boundary, including the outer current_step copy versus frame.state.current_step when present.

Should fix — Step 10 says to remove _retry_family_base without replacing its live use in _is_failed_retry_family_frame, which validate_write_root_bindings calls for managed write-root retry exemptions (calls.py:65–77,400–425). A Workflow Lisp retry with a managed write root would crash or be reported as a binding collision. Move this exemption onto the new typed lineage before deleting the helper, and test a managed-root retry.

The plan would invent a normative twelve-reason contract and mark it designed without the required design review. Complete or explicitly supersede that design gate first, and reconcile specs/state.md:274, which currently requires terminal resumes to clear current_step, with the proposed forensic preservation.

Tests go in a new tests/test_loader_import_aliases.py and run through WorkflowLoader.load, with build_loaded_workflow_bundle patched to fail if called. Cases: duplicate keys; a merge inside imports; repeated sections with a shared alias; repeated sections with distinct aliases; top-level merge sources; a single merged section that still loads. Files: orchestrator/workflow/yaml_import_aliases.py, orchestrator/loader.py, tests/test_loader_import_aliases.py.

4. Projection support data. Add an import_alias field to CallBoundaryProjection. It is keyword-constructible and defaults to None, so existing constructors keep working. In register_call_boundary (lowering.py), populate it from the call step's authored `call` alias. Add an optional max_iterations to IterationStepKeyProjection and populate it in register_repeat_until from the step's max_iterations, because the auditor needs the declared exhaustion range and must not re-read the workflow. Confirm that CallBoundaryProjection exposes the boundary's presentation step name; the embedded call_step_name check in step 8 needs it, so add it next to import_alias if it is missing. Tests in tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py: boundary alias and name (top-level and loop-contained), repeat_until max_iterations, and call_boundary_runtime_step_id unchanged. Files: orchestrator/workflow/state_projection.py, orchestrator/workflow/lowering.py, tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py.

5. Loop bookkeeping validation (item 3). New module orchestrator/workflow/resume_loop_progress.py (under 500 lines). It defines ResumeProjectionValidationError(ValueError) with .reason and .message, where str() is the message; state_projection.py re-exports it. It also defines pure validators over the raw state dict: validate_for_each_progress(name, progress) and validate_repeat_until_progress(name, progress, max_iterations, loop_step_row). For for_each: indices are unique non-boolean non-negative integers within items; current_index is in range and not already completed. A non-mapping container or entry, or an entry without a list `items`, reaches its message here, because step 9 stops RunState.from_dict from crashing on those shapes. For repeat_until, the validator admits exactly four forms: active; terminal condition success; successful exhaustion with exhausted:true and a completed loop step; failed exhaustion with exhausted absent or false and a failed loop step whose error.type is repeat_until_iterations_exhausted. Every message is the exact literal listed under enumerate_resume_slots. Each validator returns the iteration indices whose loop-local candidates exist. Tests: one table-driven test per message plus one per admitted form, in tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py through enumerate_resume_slots (step 6). Files: orchestrator/workflow/resume_loop_progress.py, orchestrator/workflow/state_projection.py, tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py.

6. Slot index and resolvers on WorkflowStateProjection. To keep state_projection.py under 500 lines, put the frozen dataclasses (ResumeProjectionSlot with node_id, step_id, presentation_key, region, iteration_index; ResumeProjectionSlotIndex; ResumeIdentityResolution; ResumeCallBoundaryResolution) and the enumeration logic in a new module, orchestrator/workflow/resume_slots.py, with thin methods on WorkflowStateProjection. enumerate_resume_slots(state) works as follows. Build candidates for top-level and finalization entries from the projection tables. Then build loop-local and loop-contained call candidates, only for iterations the step 5 validators admit, using projection.step_key, runtime_step_id and CallBoundaryProjection.runtime_step_id(i); no id string is parsed. Build call_boundaries_by_step_id. Collect unclaimed_explicit_rows as (row name, snapshotted step_id) pairs: steps.* rows with an explicit step_id that no candidate's presentation key claims. This must tolerate unhashable ids. The method never mutates or backfills state. resolve_resume_step_id(slot_index, step_id, presentation_key=None): an unhashable or malformed id resolves to count 0; with presentation_key it also reports exact_identity_candidate_count. resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, call_step_id) takes positional arguments. Tests: valid, stale, loop-local, finalization, loop-contained call and unhashable ids, plus a no-mutation assertion (deepcopy equality). Files: orchestrator/workflow/resume_slots.py, orchestrator/workflow/state_projection.py, tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py.

7. Visit families and retry lineage (item 4). New module orchestrator/workflow/resume_retry_lineage.py. It contains RetryFrameMember (frame_id, ordinal), CompletedFrameMember (frame_id), CallFrameRetryLineage (base_frame_id, completed_members, failed_predecessors in ordinal order, running_member), CallFrameRetryLineageError(ValueError) with .reason, index_retry_lineage(boundary_step_id, frame_items, *, frontend_kind) and next_unused_retry_frame_id(lineage). Frame ids are parsed relative to the local frame segment, never across the whole id. frame_id_with_overrides prefixes nested frames with their parent frame id (calls.py:157-178), so a frame id is `[<parent frame id>.]<boundary_step_id>::visit::<m>[::retry::<n>]`. The local segment is everything after the last `::visit::`. It must match `<m>` or `<m>::retry::<n>`, with m and n positive decimal integers. Ancestor `::retry::` markers before the local `::visit::` belong to the base and are not parsed, so `root.call::visit::1::retry::1.inner::visit::1::retry::2` is ordinal 2 of base `root.call::visit::1::retry::1.inner::visit::1`. Two retry markers inside the local segment are a nested marker and raise unsupported_shape. index_retry_lineage indexes one visit family (one base). Add group_visit_families(boundary_step_id, frame_items) -> tuple of VisitFamily(base_frame_id, visit_ordinal, frame_items), ordered by the typed visit ordinal, never by mapping order. A malformed visit segment raises unsupported_shape. Add select_active_family(lineages): at most one family across the boundary may have a running member, otherwise ambiguous_resumable_call_frame (the count is the number of running frames). The active family is the one with the running member; failing that, the highest-visit family that has non-completed members; failing that, None. Older families stay validated and are never resumed. This keeps a goto-revisited call valid: `root.call::visit::1` and `root.call::visit::2` coexist, and the second visit is not labelled ambiguous. Other mappings: mixed bases passed to index_retry_lineage, several running members, a duplicate ordinal, or several non-completed frames in one family of a non-Workflow-Lisp boundary raise ambiguous_resumable_call_frame. A missing ordinal or an unknown status raises unsupported_shape. A call_step_id that is not the boundary raises missing_call_boundary. Differing aliases raise persisted_import_alias_mismatch. The next retry id is the lowest unused positive ordinal over all members of the family, completed ones included. Re-export everything from resume_projection_integrity (step 8). Tests (new tests/test_resume_retry_lineage.py): each reason; ordinal ordering; idempotent allocation; a completed frame filling a gap; the single running member of a non-Workflow-Lisp boundary; two goto visit families, one older and failed and one current; two running members across visits (ambiguous); a nested child inside a parent retry frame that parses correctly; and a doubled local retry marker that is rejected. Files: orchestrator/workflow/resume_retry_lineage.py, tests/test_resume_retry_lineage.py.

8. Auditor module (items 1, 2, 7), recursive over persisted frames. New module orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py (under 500 lines). It imports nothing that loads files, computes checksums or reads migration evidence. Contents: ResumeScopePath (frozen; root(), child(), projection_scope, as_context(); a list input is snapshotted to a tuple in __post_init__); ResumeProjectionIntegrityError(ValueError) with .error; and one _diagnostic(reason, scope_path, bundle, state, field, offending_value, candidate_count, call_boundary_step_id) builder that emits all eight context keys and nulls container values. audit_scope(bundle, state, scope_path) checks, in order: (1) the shapes of steps, call_frames and each frame. (2) enumerate_resume_slots, with ResumeProjectionValidationError mapped to unsupported_shape or invalid_loop_progress. (3) Each present steps.<name>.step_id: unknown, presentation mismatch or unclaimed. An absent id stays compatible and nothing is backfilled. (4) current_step.step_id: missing_required_identity, out_of_scope or presentation mismatch. (5) For each call frame: (a) call_step_id, through one resolve_call_boundary per caller identity (missing or out-of-scope, missing_call_boundary, ambiguous_call_boundary). (b) The embedded identities that _CallFrameStateManager._snapshot writes (call_frame_state.py:169-182): frame['call_frame_id'] must equal the mapping key (unsupported_shape, field call_frames.<id>.call_frame_id, the embedded id, candidate_count null). frame['call_step_name'] must equal the resolved boundary's presentation name (presentation_slot_mismatch, field call_frames.<id>.call_step_name, the name, 1). The outer frame['current_step'] copy must equal frame['state']['current_step'] when both are present (unsupported_shape, field call_frames.<id>.current_step, offending value null). (c) import_alias against boundary.import_alias. (d) The boundary alias must be present in the bundle imports (missing_imported_bundle). (e) group_visit_families, index_retry_lineage per family and select_active_family, all with the imported bundle's frontend_kind. (6) Recursion: every non-completed frame (running members and failed predecessors, in every visit family) is audited with audit_scope(imports[boundary.import_alias], frame['state'], scope_path.child(frame_id)), calling through the module-global name, and so on down the tree. Completed frames get only the frame-level checks of (5). As a result, a stale callee-local identity already persisted in any resumable or predecessor frame fails the root audit, before any visit, start or result publication, with the three-field root envelope (finding 1). Reached calls still revalidate (step 10) to defend against races. Re-export the step 7 lineage API. Tests (new tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py, behavioural, through audit_scope on loaded temp workflows): one test per reason, checking field, offending_value and candidate_count; mismatches of the embedded call_frame_id, call_step_name and current_step copy; a two-level nested stale callee-local id, caught with a two-element scope_path; a stale id in a failed predecessor; a privacy test that bound inputs, context values and container contents never appear in the JSON-dumped error; a no-mutation test; and a static test that the module source does not import the parity or retirement modules and contains no forbidden identifiers or strings (receipt, or cache together with audit / resume projection / projection integrity). Files: orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py, tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py.

9. StateManager decode boundary, raw patches and envelopes (items 1, 6). (a) Tolerant decode. StateManager.load runs RunState.from_dict before either audit. Today from_dict raises KeyError on a missing workflow_file or workflow_checksum and runs ForEachState(**...) on every for_each value (state.py:153-188), so these shapes never reach the guard. Change from_dict: read workflow_file and workflow_checksum with .get (typed Optional[str]). Keep a non-mapping for_each container, or a non-mapping entry, as its raw value; to_dict already passes non-ForEachState values through. Build ForEachState from the known fields of a mapping entry, and keep the raw dict when items is missing, so that step 5's messages classify it. Now missing_workflow_path and missing_recorded_checksum reach the executor's checksum envelope, and a malformed for_each reaches audit_scope as unsupported_shape. State this decode rule in specs/state.md. New runs always set both fields, and runtime code reads for_each only after the audit has accepted it. (b) Add one public update_root_fields(updates: Mapping[str, Any]). Under the lock it reads the raw state.json dict, sets only the given root keys, sets updated_at, writes atomically with _write_json_atomic and then refreshes self.state. Unknown root fields and the run tree are preserved. (c) Add record_workflow_checksum_mismatch(*, workflow_file, persisted_checksum, current_checksum, reason), which validates reason against the four literals, and record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(error). Both go through update_root_fields with only status='failed' and error, so current_step is left untouched (unlike fail_run). Tests in tests/test_state_manager.py: a before/after diff of state.json shows only status, error and updated_at changed, with an unknown root key preserved; update_root_fields changes only its keys; load succeeds on state without a workflow_checksum, on state without a workflow_file, and on a malformed for_each container or entry; pre-v2.0 state is still rejected. Files: orchestrator/state.py, tests/test_state_manager.py.

10. Reached-call integration (items 1, 4, 6). Add `from .resume_projection_integrity import audit_scope` at module level in calls.py (tests substitute this name). Keep the new logic in a helper module, orchestrator/workflow/call_resume_audit.py, so calls.py does not grow much past its current 982 lines. Replace the resume scan in frame_id_with_overrides (calls.py:141-152), which returns the first non-completed frame with the same call_step_id. On resume, execute_call does the following. (1) Compute the fresh visit frame id from step_visits without any scan. Before any lineage grouping, reject a completed frame stored under that key, whatever its call_step_id, using resume_state_invalid_result with detail completed_call_frame_id_collision and exactly the specified context. Step 11 makes that result sticky. (2) Call resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, call_step_id) once against the parent projection. Exactly one boundary is required, its import_alias selects the callee bundle, and the persisted alias is only checked. (3) Run the pure step 7 indexing (group_visit_families, index_retry_lineage, select_active_family) for that boundary. The frame the call occupies is the active family's running member, else next_unused_retry_frame_id of the active family (Workflow Lisp, failed predecessors only), else the fresh visit id. (4) Keep the ordinary visit/start publication and the authored/managed input, write-root, checksum and resume-bound-input validation in their current order. Move the managed write-root retry exemption onto the typed lineage. validate_write_root_bindings currently exempts prior frames through _is_failed_retry_family_frame/_retry_family_base (calls.py:65-77, 413-421); instead it exempts a prior frame exactly when that frame is a failed predecessor of the active lineage and the occupied frame is a retry member. Delete both helpers and _retry_frame_id only after that switch. (5) Then, if there is a running member, its checksum and bound-input errors win; next, checksum-validate each failed predecessor and audit it with audit_scope(..., scope_path.child(frame_id)) in ordinal order; then audit the running member's state and resume it. With no running member, validate and audit the predecessors and then allocate the retry id. All of this happens before _CallFrameStateManager or the child WorkflowExecutor exists. Carry the scope path (the frame id chain) on the executor and state manager for nested recursion. Mutation envelope: because the root audit (step 8) has already caught every pre-persisted stale identity with the three-field envelope, a reached-call failure only arises when the root audit was bypassed or raced (direct CallExecutor.execute_call, or state changing after the root audit). Its delta is item 6's reached-callee envelope, which is a different contract from the root envelope, and both are stated in specs/state.md: the caller's step_visits increment and visit/start publication, the failed call-step result carrying the exact diagnostic, current_step, ancestor frame snapshots, root status/error/updated_at, and configured finalization if it runs. The selected callee frame stays byte-identical. A child resume_projection_integrity_error passes up unwrapped, never as call_failed. Update the Task-1 characterization tests in tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py that documented the old gaps (a stale caller id starting a fresh child; the ambiguity prerequisite) to assert the new fail-closed contract; do not delete them. Add tests, through CallExecutor.execute_call: stale caller; alias mismatch; missing import; ambiguous frames; retry lineage with a running member and with only failed predecessors; a stale id in a failed predecessor; a nested two-level stale callee-local id, asserting the exact reached-callee delta field by field; a goto-revisited call whose older visit family is ignored and whose current visit resumes; a nested call inside a Workflow Lisp parent retry frame; a managed-write-root Workflow Lisp retry that is neither a crash nor a binding collision; the collision envelope; call_resume_checksum_mismatch precedence; and an ordering test that substitutes calls.audit_scope and asserts no child frame is created. Files: orchestrator/workflow/calls.py, orchestrator/workflow/call_resume_audit.py, orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_state.py, tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py.

11. Root executor guard and sticky failures (items 1, 4, 6). In executor.py, add a module-level `from .resume_projection_integrity import audit_scope`. In execute(), when resume is true and the state manager is the structural root (not a CallFrameStateManager), run the guard as the first state-touching action: before update_status('running') (executor.py:2565), any control-flow counter write, and _execute_prologue. (a) Recheck the checksum: missing_workflow_path when state.workflow_file is None, missing_recorded_checksum when workflow_checksum is None (both reachable now, step 9), workflow_unavailable when the file is missing or unreadable, and workflow_modified when it differs, computed with self.state_manager.calculate_checksum. On failure, call record_workflow_checksum_mismatch and return the persisted state. (b) Call audit_scope(self.loaded_bundle, state, ResumeScopePath.root(workflow_file)), which is recursive (step 8). On failure, call record_resume_projection_integrity_failure and return. Child executors skip both. Sticky failures: add one predicate, is_sticky_resume_failure(error). It is true for type resume_projection_integrity_error, and for the completed-frame collision contract violation (context.reason == 'call_resume_state_invalid' and context.detail == 'completed_call_frame_id_collision'), so that this persisted call-frame identity failure, kept in the task-mandated shape, cannot follow ordinary call-failure routing. Put the predicate in orchestrator/workflow/step_results.py, outside the auditor module. When the predicate holds, _handle_control_flow returns '_stop' before goto, on_error=continue and strict_flow handling. loops.py stops for_each and repeat_until continuation. _execute_step_loop promotes the step's error unchanged to the run error, and nesting promotes it unchanged to the root. finalization.py record_step_result sets failure.error to the cleanup's projection error, or null otherwise. In executor.py's finalization path and _execute_epilogue, a sticky run error is never replaced or cleared: neither _finalization_failure_error nor the completed-path state.pop('error') may touch it. A projection error that arises only in finalization becomes the run error. Tests (the direct-executor section of tests/test_resume_command.py, and tests/test_structured_control_flow.py): the checksum envelope for each of the four reasons with a three-field diff; a stale callee-local id persisted two frames deep gives the three-field root envelope with step_visits unchanged; success, failure and always routes, on_error=continue and loop continuation all stop, both for the projection error and for the collision violation; a finalization failure is supplemental; a projection error inside finalization only; and an ordering test that substitutes executor.audit_scope and asserts it runs before update_status and the prologue. Files: orchestrator/workflow/executor.py, orchestrator/workflow/step_results.py, orchestrator/workflow/loops.py, orchestrator/workflow/finalization.py, tests/test_resume_command.py, tests/test_structured_control_flow.py.

12. Resume CLI ordering and race envelope (items 1, 6). In orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py, add a module-level `from orchestrator.workflow.resume_projection_integrity import ResumeScopePath, ResumeProjectionIntegrityError, audit_scope`. Move the observability-override persistence (resume.py:403-406) from before the workflow load to after the checksum check and the audit. For a non-force-restart resume, call audit_scope(workflow_bundle, state.to_dict(), ResumeScopePath.root(state.workflow_file)) after the checksum check and before observability persistence, open_executor_session, write_process_metadata and WorkflowExecutor construction. On ResumeProjectionIntegrityError, call state_manager.record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(exc.error), print the reason to stderr and return 1. The initial checksum precheck keeps exit 1 with nothing written; moving the observability write is what makes 'nothing written' true. Route the three CLI writes that follow a passing audit (observability override, open_executor_session at 547, close_executor_session in finally at 616-621) through update_root_fields with only {'observability': ...} or {'runtime_observability': ...}, instead of _write_state. Today _write_state serializes RunState.to_dict, which drops unknown root keys and rewrites the whole root. The race envelope is then exactly specified, and stated in specs/state.md: relative to the state written just before executor.execute, the second-audit failure changes only status, error and updated_at, and the finally-block session close afterwards changes only runtime_observability.executor_sessions. Relative to the pre-resume state.json, the full delta is those fields, plus observability when overrides were given, plus the opened-then-failed-closed session; process metadata lives outside state.json. Unknown root keys survive throughout, and the close never replaces the diagnostic. Update test_projection_resume_integrity_mutation_order_cli_root_explicit_id_corruption and its siblings to assert the new envelope. Add: an ordering test that substitutes resume.audit_scope and records the call order against open_executor_session and WorkflowExecutor; the checksum precheck writing nothing even with observability overrides; a race test (the CLI audit passes and the executor's second audit fails) asserting both deltas above exactly, with an unknown root key preserved, the session closed as failed and the diagnostic preserved; a stale id persisted in an existing child frame failing at the CLI with a three-field diff; and pre-v2.0 and pre-2.1 call state still rejected. Files: orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py, tests/test_resume_command.py.

13. Forensic current_step in observability (item 6; the specs/state.md:274 exception from step 1). Add one predicate, is_forensic_current_step(state), in orchestrator/runtime_observability.py: status is failed and error.type is in {resume_projection_integrity_error, workflow_checksum_mismatch}. Use it at each reader. In build_status_snapshot (orchestrator/observability/report.py), a forensic current step is not treated as current: it shows status and summary pending and current_visit_count null, and counts under pending; render_status_markdown never calls it 'in progress'. Use the same predicate in the monitor (orchestrator/monitor/classifier.py _active_cursor_heartbeat, orchestrator/monitor/messages.py _heartbeat_at) and the dashboard (the heartbeat/started_at helpers in orchestrator/dashboard/projection.py), so they report no live heartbeat and no stalled run for it. Tests: tests/test_observability_report.py (snapshot and markdown), tests/test_monitor_classifier.py, tests/test_dashboard_projection.py. Files: orchestrator/runtime_observability.py, orchestrator/observability/report.py, orchestrator/monitor/classifier.py, orchestrator/monitor/messages.py, orchestrator/dashboard/projection.py, tests/test_observability_report.py, tests/test_monitor_classifier.py, tests/test_dashboard_projection.py.

14. Verification and docs closeout. Run pytest --collect-only on every new or renamed test module. Run the narrow selectors per step. Then run the dev-check.json suite (tests/test_workflow_state_compatibility.py, test_at68_resume_force_restart.py, test_runtime_failure_persistence.py, and the lexical checkpoint, migration-parity and identity-retirement tests), then tests/test_state_manager.py, test_resume_command.py, test_subworkflow_calls.py, test_resume_retry_lineage.py, test_resume_projection_integrity.py, test_workflow_state_projection.py, test_loader_validation.py, test_loader_import_aliases.py and test_workflow_lisp_examples.py. Resume runtime changed, so run one orchestrator end-to-end smoke check from the repo root, in tmux under the ptycho311 env if it is long. Run a demo workflow containing a call step and interrupt it during the callee; `orchestrator resume <run_id>` succeeds. Then, with the checksum unchanged, corrupt one root steps.*.step_id, and separately one step_id inside the persisted call frame's state. Each time, `orchestrator resume` must exit 1 with resume_projection_integrity_error and a three-field state diff (step_visits unchanged). Set the docs/capability_status_matrix.md entry to implemented, set the design doc status to implemented, and confirm that the selectors in specs/acceptance/index.md match the real test names. Commit in steps, one commit per step above, never with --no-verify. Files: docs/capability_status_matrix.md, docs/design/resume_projection_integrity_hardening.md, specs/acceptance/index.md, docs/plans/2026-10-18-resume-projection-integrity-implementation-plan.md.
